title: Fully dynamic matching · keep the edges
scope: General unweighted graphs under online edge insertions and deletions; explicitly maintained matching edges.
ratioDefinition: β = |M| / OPT. Larger is better. Hollow markers show limiting approximation endpoints, not attained guarantees.
assumptions: General unweighted graphs; n fixed vertices.
Both edge insertions and deletions; online updates.
Each row retains its adversary, randomization and update-time convention.
ε is any fixed positive accuracy parameter unless stated otherwise.
m and Δ bounds are preserved, without substituting sparse or dense graphs.

headline.note: Deterministic polylogarithmic worst-case updates approach β=1/2. Exact β=1/2 is available with O(1) expected amortized time against oblivious updates.

openQuestions: Can a fixed improvement β>1/2 be maintained explicitly in polylogarithmic update time on general graphs?
Can β=1−ε, for every fixed ε>0, be maintained explicitly with unconditional n^{1−δ} update time for a fixed δ>0?

results.title: Simple Deterministic Algorithms for Fully Dynamic Maximal Matching
results.sourceLocation: §1, Our results; §3 maximality and no length-3 augmenting path
results.statement: Deterministically maintains a maximal matching with no augmenting path of length three, ensuring at least 2/3 of optimum.
results.notes: The 2/3 guarantee is attained. The paper suppresses additive logarithmic terms in n; its short version details O(√(m+n)) and states O(√m) for the full version.

results.title: Fully Dynamic (1+ε)-Approximate Matchings
results.statement: Maintains a (1+ε)-approximate maximum-cardinality matching under insertions and deletions.
results.notes: Retain √m: it becomes n on dense graphs but √n on sparse graphs. The endpoint β=1 is not attained by a fixed ε>0.

results.title: Fully Dynamic Maximal Matching in Constant Update Time
results.statement: Maintains an exact maximal matching with O(t) expected total time over t updates from an empty graph.
results.notes: Maximal means no edge can be added; it need not be maximum. Every maximal matching has at least half the optimum cardinality.

results.title: Deterministic Dynamic Matching in Worst-Case Update Time
results.statement: Maintains an explicit (2+ε)-approximate matching with deterministic worst-case polylogarithmic update time.
results.notes: O_ε hides polynomial dependence on 1/ε. The same paper gives (3/2+ε) approximation in n^{1/2+o(1)} worst-case time.

results.title: New Trade-Offs for Fully Dynamic Matching via Hierarchical EDCS
results.statement: Maintains at least a (0.532−ε) fraction of optimum in general graphs, with high probability.
results.notes: Theorem states α(3)≥0.532. The displayed constant is a certified lower bound, not the exact optimum of its factor-revealing analysis.

results.title: New Trade-Offs for Fully Dynamic Matching via Hierarchical EDCS
results.statement: Maintains at least a (0.609−ε) fraction of optimum in general graphs, with high probability.
results.notes: The better constants 0.612 and 0.563 in this paper require bipartite graphs and are excluded here.

results.title: Maintaining an EDCS in General Graphs: Simpler, Density-Sensitive and with Worst-Case Time Bounds
results.authors: Fabrizio Grandoni, Chris Schwiegelshohn, Shay Solomon, Amitai Uzrad
results.statement: Maintains a (3/2+ε)-approximate matching deterministically, for ε<1/2.
results.notes: On graphs with arboricity a, the bound improves to O(√a ε^{−5/2}+ε^{−6}). The common √n specialization uses only m≤n².

results.title: On Regularity Lemma and Barriers in Streaming and Dynamic Matching
results.authors: Sepehr Assadi, Soheil Behnezhad, Sanjeev Khanna, Huan Li
results.statement: Maintains a (1−o(1))-approximate matching with high probability in slightly sublinear worst-case update time.
results.notes: The improvement is an iterated-log factor; it does not establish a fixed sublinear polynomial exponent.

results.title: Improved Bounds for Fully Dynamic Matching via Ordered Ruzsa-Szemerédi Graphs
results.authors: Sepehr Assadi, Sanjeev Khanna, Peter Kiss
results.statement: Maintains a (1−ε)-approximate matching with high probability; the runtime is governed by ordered Ruzsa–Szemerédi graphs.
results.notes: ORS(n) suppresses a linear matching-size parameter depending on accuracy and hierarchy depth. Its value is unknown; no fixed n-exponent is assigned here.

orsInterval.meaning: Image of the published ORS range under this algorithm's upper-bound formula. The left endpoint is not an update-time lower bound. Hidden constants and the matching-size coefficient c depend on the theorem; bar lengths are schematic.
orsInterval.displayNote: Leading-power shorthand for F(L) and F(U), at fixed ε and δ; original ε prefactors and exact symbolic substitutions are retained. These are envelopes for the theorem-bound expression, not a tight interval for actual running time.

results.title: A Framework for Boosting Matching Approximation: Parallel, Distributed, and Dynamic
results.statement: Maintains a (1+ε)-approximate maximum matching on general graphs against adaptive adversaries.
results.notes: Improves the ε-dependence of general-graph boosting. This is slightly sublinear, not n^{1−δ} for a fixed δ>0. The separate n^{0.58} theorem is offline and excluded.

results.title: A Faster Deterministic Algorithm for Fully Dynamic Maximal Matching
results.authors: Julia Chuzhoy, Sanjeev Khanna, Junkai Song
results.statement: Maintains an exact maximal matching deterministically from an initially empty graph.
results.notes: This improves the exact-maximality task under adaptive updates; it does not improve the β=1/2 approximation ratio.

results.title: A Faster Deterministic Algorithm for Fully Dynamic Maximal Matching
results.authors: Julia Chuzhoy, Sanjeev Khanna, Junkai Song
results.statement: The authors state that substituting randomized edge coloring improves their maximal-matching update time to Õ(√n) against adaptive updates.
results.notes: Kept separate from the deterministic n^{1/2+o(1)} theorem.

results.title: Fully Dynamic Matching and Ordered Ruzsa-Szemerédi Graphs
results.statement: For every fixed ε>0, maintains the edges of a (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching in Õ(√(n^{1+ε} · ORSₙ(Θ(ε²n)))) amortized update time, against adaptive adversaries.
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1, printed page 2 (PDF page 4); §4 probability analysis
results.notes: ORSₙ(r) is the maximum number of ordered induced matchings, each of size r, on n vertices. Theorem 1 retains r=Θ(ε²n). A fixed polynomial update exponent is not known without an additional ORS bound. The algorithm is randomized and supports adaptive updates; the update bound is amortized.

orsInterval.meaning: Image of the published ORS range under this algorithm's upper-bound formula. The left endpoint is not an update-time lower bound. Hidden constants and the matching-size coefficient c depend on the theorem; bar lengths are schematic.
orsInterval.factorNote: R = ORSₙ(Θ(ε²n)); c depends on ε
orsInterval.displayNote: Leading-power shorthand for F(L) and F(U), at fixed ε and δ; original ε prefactors and exact symbolic substitutions are retained. These are envelopes for the theorem-bound expression, not a tight interval for actual running time.

relatedResults.title: New Deterministic Approximation Algorithms for Fully Dynamic Matching
relatedResults.authors: Sayan Bhattacharya, Monika Henzinger, Danupon Nanongkai
relatedResults.statement: Maintains an explicit (2+ε)-approximate maximum matching deterministically.
relatedResults.notes: A landmark deterministic polylogarithmic update bound; ε=0 is not included.

relatedResults.title: A Framework for Boosting Matching Approximation: Parallel, Distributed, and Dynamic
relatedResults.statement: For any fixed δ>0, improves the accuracy dependence to (1/ε)^{O(1/δ)}·n^δ·ORS(n,Θ_{δ,ε}(n)) for β=1/(1+ε), amortized against adaptive updates. The earlier poly(1/ε)·n^{o(1)} formulation was corrected.
relatedResults.notes: δ>0 is a fixed runtime parameter. Uses the corrected full-version statement; polynomial ε-dependence and n^{o(1)} cannot be asserted simultaneously.

orsInterval.meaning: Image of the published ORS range under this algorithm's upper-bound formula. The left endpoint is not an update-time lower bound. Hidden constants and the matching-size coefficient c depend on the theorem; bar lengths are schematic.
orsInterval.displayNote: Leading-power shorthand for F(L) and F(U), at fixed ε and δ; original ε prefactors and exact symbolic substitutions are retained. These are envelopes for the theorem-bound expression, not a tight interval for actual running time.

relatedResults.title: Fully Dynamic Matching: Beating 2-Approximation in Δ^ε Update Time
relatedResults.statement: For every constant δ>0, obtains β=1/(2−Ω_δ(1)) in O(Δ^δ+polylog n) worst-case time, randomized against an oblivious adversary. The improvement constant depends on δ.
relatedResults.authors: Soheil Behnezhad, Jakub Łącki, Vahab Mirrokni
relatedResults.notes: δ denotes the exponent called ε in the paper. The positive approximation improvement depends on δ.

relatedResults.title: New Trade-Offs for Fully Dynamic Matching via Hierarchical EDCS
relatedResults.statement: For integer k≥0: β=α(k)−ε and update min{Δ^{1/(k+1)},m^{1/(2k+2)}}·poly(k,1/ε,log n), worst-case and oblivious. α(0)=1, α(1)=2/3; higher levels approach 1/2.
relatedResults.notes: α(0)=1 and α(1)=2/3; the paper uses α as a retained fraction, whereas this atlas calls that quantity β.

relatedResults.title: Rounding Dynamic Matchings Against an Adaptive Adversary
relatedResults.statement: Theorem 1.2 gives β=1/(2+ε) and poly(1/ε) amortized time against adaptive updates, with both approximation and update bounds in expectation. Theorem 1.1 instead gives a Las Vegas worst-case polylogarithmic bound with high probability.
relatedResults.notes: This row describes Theorem 1.2. Theorem 1.1 gives a Las Vegas poly(log n,1/ε) worst-case bound with high probability; it is a separate guarantee.

relatedResults.title: Deterministic Dynamic Maximal Matching in Sublinear Update Time
relatedResults.statement: Earlier exact-maximality breakthrough: Õ(n^{8/9}) deterministic or Õ(n^{3/4}) randomized adaptive amortized update time. Superseded in n-dependence by Chuzhoy–Khanna–Song 2026.
relatedResults.authors: Aaron Bernstein, Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss, Thatchaphol Saranurak
relatedResults.notes: Two variants with different randomization guarantees; both maintain exact maximality.

relatedResults.title: On Approximate Fully-Dynamic Matching and Online Matrix-Vector Multiplication
relatedResults.statement: The original poly(1/ε)·n/2^{Ω(√log n)} near-optimal matching theorem is stated for bipartite graphs. The general-graph row above uses the later Mitrović–Sheu result.
relatedResults.notes: Bipartite input. The distinct offline theorem is excluded from the online landscape.

relatedResults.title: Fully Dynamic Maximal Matching in O(log n) Update Time (Corrected Version)
relatedResults.statement: Exact maximal matching in O(log n) expected amortized update time against oblivious updates. The corrected analysis preserves this bound; Solomon later improves it to O(1).
relatedResults.authors: Surender Baswana, Manoj Gupta, Sandeep Sen
relatedResults.notes: Uses the corrected analysis. The high-probability total-time guarantee includes an additive n log² n term.

relatedResults.title: Faster Fully Dynamic Matchings with Small Approximation Ratios
relatedResults.statement: Explicit (3/2+ε)-approximate matching with deterministic O(m^{1/4} ε^{−5/2}) amortized update time. GSSU 2022 achieves the same m-exponent with a worst-case guarantee.
relatedResults.notes: Main general-graph theorem; specialized bounded-arboricity bounds are separate.

relatedResults.title: Unifying and Strengthening Hardness for Dynamic Problems via the Online Matrix-Vector Multiplication Conjecture
relatedResults.updateTime: No simultaneous m^{1/2−δ} updates and m^{1−δ} queries
relatedResults.sourceLocation: Corollary 3.4 and following reductions; Table 5 footnote
relatedResults.statement: Under the OMv conjecture, polynomial preprocessing cannot coexist with update time m^{1/2-delta} and query time m^{1-delta} for fixed delta>0 for exact bipartite perfect matching or exact maximum-matching size. The fully dynamic lower bound allows amortized updates; the corresponding partially dynamic statement is worst-case.
relatedResults.summary: Applies to exact matching size or perfect-matching detection. It does not rule out the constant-factor approximations above.
relatedResults.notes: At dense m=Theta(n^2), this excludes truly sublinear-in-n updates when queries are sufficiently fast. The reduction distinguishes exact matching sizes; it is not a constant-factor approximation lower bound.

coverage: Selected principal tradeoffs and historical milestones, checked against primary theorem statements. This is a research map, not a completeness certificate for every bound or graph subclass.
